speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your symptoms, have you noticed any pain in your abdomen, particularly on the right side under your ribs?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 year...

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you experienced any fever or chills, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or appetite beyond the weight loss? I would like to order some initial blood work to assess your liver function and rule out infection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results show a cholestatic pattern with elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase but normal transaminases, which suggests an obstruction rather than hepatitis. Given your age, weight loss, and painless jaundice, I need to know if you have experienced any unintended weight loss beyond what you mentioned, and have you noticed any swelling in your legs or abdomen?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_Ultrasound: Anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region. Dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound findings of a cystic mass in the subhepatic region with biliary dilation strongly suggest a choledochal cyst causing obstruction. To further characterize the anatomy and rule out malignancy, I need to visualize the biliary tree more clearly.

REQUEST TEST: MRCP
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unexpected, as the ultrasound clearly showed biliary dilation and a cystic mass, which MRCP should have visualized. Let me clarify: did the MRCP report state that the biliary tree was normal, or did it fail to visualize the mass seen on ultrasound? I need to reconcile these conflicting imaging results before proceeding.

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the smoking history and painless obstructive jaundice, I suspect a malignancy that may have been missed or misinterpreted on the MRCP. I will request a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast to better characterize the mass and look for signs of pancreatic or biliary cancer.

REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis_Contrast

speaker: Doctor
text:
This is highly unusual, as both the ultrasound and clinical picture strongly suggest an obstructive process, yet advanced imaging like MRCP and CT are normal. I need to verify if there is a palpable mass or gallbladder distension on physical exam to guide further invasive testing.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledochal cyst
